_meta.indication: SUNLENCA, in combination with other antiretroviral(s), is indicated for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in heavily treatment-experienced adults with multidrug resistant HIV-1 infection failing their current antiretroviral regimen due to resistance, intolerance, or safety considerations.

pivotal_trials.design: Partially randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind multicenter trial; Cohort 1 randomized 2:1 (LEN:placebo) and blinded during the functional monotherapy period (FMP), then open-label maintenance; Cohort 2 single-arm, open-label.
pivotal_trials.population: Heavily treatment-experienced (HTE) adults with multidrug-resistant (MDR) HIV-1 infection failing their current regimen due to resistance, intolerance, or safety considerations.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary: proportion of subjects in Cohort 1 achieving a reduction in HIV-1 RNA of ≥0.5 log10 copies/mL from baseline at the end of the functional monotherapy period (FMP) at Day 14.
pivotal_trials.n: N=72 treated (Cohort 1: 36 [Cohort 1A LEN N=24, Cohort 1B PBO N=12]; Cohort 2: 36)
pivotal_trials.result: Primary endpoint met: 87.5% of SUNLENCA subjects (N=24) vs 16.7% of placebo (N=12) achieved ≥0.5 log10 decrease in viral load at end of FMP; treatment difference 70.8% (95% CI 34.9% to 90.0%). At Week 52, 83.3% of Cohort 1 achieved HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥3%, all grades) were injection site reactions (65%) and nausea (4%). Injection site reactions were the most frequent AE; nodules and indurations may persist. 96% of adverse reactions were mild or moderate; 1% discontinued SUNLENCA due to an AE (Grade 1 injection site nodule).
target_moa: First-in-class, multistage selective inhibitor of HIV-1 capsid function that directly binds the interface between capsid protein (p24) subunits in hexamers, inhibiting HIV-1 replication.

advisory_committee.vote: This application was not taken to an FDA advisory committee because the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues that were unexpected.

On 20 March, 2018, Gilead submitted a new IND 138311 for lenacapavir tablets, for the treatment of HIV-1 infection and the Agency deemed the IND safe to proceed on 19 April, 2018. Fast Track Designation was granted on 19 September, 2018 for the treatment of HIV-1 infection.

basis.text: The application received Priority review designation.

summary.text: Lenacapavir (SUNLENCA), a first-in-class HIV-1 capsid inhibitor, received Fast Track Designation (2018) and Breakthrough Therapy Designation (May 30, 2019) for HTE patients with MDR HIV-1, and was reviewed under Priority review. It was approved via traditional approval based on the CAPELLA primary endpoint after a first-cycle Complete Response Letter (Feb 28, 2022) for product quality deficiencies and a June 27, 2022 resubmission.

citations.quote: LEN is a first-in-class human immunodeficiency type 1 (HIV-1) capsid inhibitor with Breakthrough Therapy Designation.
